subject.title: Active user message keeps inbound metadata that history strips, breaking prompt-cache byte-stability every turn

question: Should the fix preserve current inbound metadata through a stable runtime-context channel before stripping active user text, or may active turns stop exposing that metadata to the model?
rationale: The source shows the metadata is current-turn AI-facing context today, so automation cannot safely choose the compatibility trade-off for reply and channel behavior.

options.title: Require context handoff before merge
options.body: Move or stack the current inbound metadata into runtime context before stripping active user text, keeping both cache stability and model-visible context.

options.title: Accept active metadata removal
options.body: Land the cache fix while intentionally removing inline current-turn metadata from provider input, with explicit maintainer sign-off and live channel proof.

options.title: Use the runtime-context PR as canonical
options.body: Pause this issue's linked PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89428 or an equivalent context handoff is decided.

recommendation.title: Require context handoff before merge
recommendation.body: Move or stack the current inbound metadata into runtime context before stripping active user text, keeping both cache stability and model-visible context.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle merged the prior cache-stability boundary change and is the strongest history signal for the compatibility choice.
